subject: Maths
title: Geometric sequences
subtitle: Sequences · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can identify, generate, and find the nth term of geometric sequences.

key_vocab.definition: A geometric sequence has a constant common ratio (r) between consecutive terms. Each term is found by multiplying the previous term by r.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can identify, generate, and find the nth term of geometric sequences.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: geometric sequence -- A geometric sequence has a constant common ratio (r) between consecutive terms. Each term is found by multiplying the previous term by r.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Divide consecutive terms to find r. The nth term formula is un = arn−1.
un = a × rn−1
a = first term, r = common ratio, n = term number

Key examples:
  ✓ 2, 6, 18, 54, ... (r = 3)  (multiply by 3)
  ✓ 100, 50, 25, 12.5, ... (r = 0.5)  (multiply by &frac{1}{2})
  ✓ un = 3 × 2n−1 gives 3, 6, 12, 24, ...  (a=3, r=2)
  ✗ 2, 4, 6, 8, ... is geometric  (that is arithmetic (+2))
  ✗ un = arn (should be n−1)  (exponent is n−1)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – finding the common ratio
  Find the common ratio of 5, 15, 45, 135, ...
  r = second ÷ first = 15 ÷ 5 = 3
  Check: 45 ÷ 15 = 3, 135 ÷ 45 = 3
  Common ratio r = 3
  r = 3
  (Divide any term by the previous term to find r.)

Example 2 – finding the nth term
  Find the 8th term of 2, 6, 18, 54, ...
  a = 2, r = 3
  u8 = 2 × 37
  u8 = 2 × 2187 = 4374
  u8 = 4374
  (Use un = arn−1 with careful power calculation.)

sections.title: Finding specific terms
sections.content:
Use un = arn−1 to find the stated term.

(a) a = 2, r = 3. Find u6.
(b) a = 5, r = 2. Find u8.
(c) a = 100, r = 0.5. Find u5.
(d) a = 1, r = 10. Find u4.

sections.title: Mixed geometric problems
sections.content:
Answer each question.

(a) 3rd term = 12, r = 2. Find the 1st term.
(b) 1st term = 5, 4th term = 40. Find r.
(c) Sequence: 2, 6, 18, ... Which term is 1458?
(d) a = 1000, r = 0.8. Find u3.
(e) Sum of first 4 terms of 1, 2, 4, 8, ...

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ In a geometric sequence, you multiply by the same ratio each time
✗ 2, 4, 6, 8 is a geometric sequence
✓ The nth term is un = arn−1
✗ The nth term is un = arn
✓ A negative ratio causes terms to alternate in sign
